text: DREAM RULEBOOK
title: dream rulebook

text:
WHY DREAMRULES?

We made Dreamrules to keep what makes Dune compelling: distinct factions, hidden information, negotiation and battles that can turn on one decision. We wanted to address the rules that can leave players waiting for the game to end, and give every faction more meaningful choices.

Balance, mastery and counterplay

Our goals are balance between factions, a high skill ceiling and counterplay to every powerful effect. Balance does not mean making factions alike. Each should have a credible route to victory, with strengths worth exploiting and weaknesses opponents can challenge.

A high skill ceiling means there is room to improve through reading the board, managing resources, judging opponents and negotiating well. Counterplay means a strong move should leave opponents some way to respond, whether through cards, positioning, information or a deal.

Ending the Guild stallout

In GF9, the Guild can win by preventing anyone else from winning before the game ends. That creates an incentive to run out the clock. Too many games drag on as a result, and the waiting makes them less fun.

Dreamrules removes that Guild victory condition. The Guild keeps its shipping economy and gains other tools, including Retreat, but cannot win simply by keeping everyone else from winning. The aim is a game that rewards pursuing a victory rather than prolonging a stalemate.

What stays familiar

Dreamrules builds on GF9's Advanced Game. Spice, troop support in battle, hidden battle plans, traitors, alliances and stronghold control remain central. This book is written for new and returning players. Familiarity with GF9 should not be required.

What changes?

Your Fate is a once-per-game faction power activated by a matching worthless Treachery Card. Fate replaces the old special faction Karama powers.

Nexus checks now use a separate deck after Storm, independent of Shai-Hulud. This gives alliance opportunities their own probability curve as the game progresses. It also lets us tune the number of worm cards to make spice collection dangerous enough and give Fremen more mobility, without changing Nexus frequency.

Spice mines supply spice over several turns. Tech tokens provide income and can contribute to victory. The Shield Wall can also become a stronghold for victory purposes.

Mercenaries adds battle strength, Supplies provides temporary combat cards, and Break Conditioning rewards an overwhelming strength advantage. The card chapter covers the revised deck.

Fremen gain full storm immunity, the Guild can pay to retreat, and Bene Tleilax use lasting Infiltration. Read your faction chapter even if you know its GF9 version.

title: Contents

text:
THE GAME
Control Arrakis

Each player leads a faction seeking control of Arrakis. Troops occupy territories, leaders command battles and spice pays for the means to expand your position. Treachery Cards can decide a fight before troop strength matters. Information and agreements can be worth as much as either.

Strongholds are the main route to victory. A lone faction normally needs three; two allies normally need four between them, checked during Mentat. Holding territory during the turn is only part of the task: you must still meet the victory condition when the game checks for a winner. Alliances allow two factions to pursue a shared victory. Bene Gesserit prediction, Bene Tleilax infiltration and the Fremen endgame condition can change who wins.

Dreamrules also gives the Shield Wall and tech tokens a role in victory. The victory chapter gives the ordinary count and the v0.8 priority between tech tokens and Shield Wall. The full interaction with Prediction and Infiltration is still tracked in #1847.

Faction advantages change the choices available to each player. Atreides can obtain information before committing to a fight. The Emperor earns spice from other players' card purchases. The Guild earns spice from shipment. Your faction chapter explains when its advantages apply and which benefits an ally can receive.

Read the board

Territories have names and boundaries. Storm sectors divide the planet radially. A territory can cross more than one sector, so a storm can cover only part of it. Keep troops in the sector they occupy; their position can matter even within one territory.

Sand territories are the open desert where spice appears and worms threaten troops. Strongholds are the principal locations players fight to control. The Polar Sink and the Shield Wall have their own rules. Do not assume every named territory behaves like a stronghold.

Your reserves hold troops available to enter play. The Tleilaxu Tanks hold dead troops and leaders awaiting revival. These are different destinations. For example, the v0.8 spice-mine rule returns troops at a destroyed mine to reserves instead of killing them.

Spice has several uses. It pays for Treachery Cards, shipment and revival, and can support troops committed to battle. Keep available spice separate from bribes waiting for Mentat and token income waiting for the end of its triggering phase. Those later payments are not yet part of your spendable supply.

A battle plan commits troops and usually a leader, with permitted weapons, defenses and other cards. A strong leader can be killed by an undefended weapon or betrayed by a traitor. The battle chapter must therefore resolve cards and special results before comparing final strength.

title: Find the strongholds

text:
PREPARE THE GAME
1. Choose which factions take part

Each player selects one faction they want included in the game. This selects the factions at the table, not who will play each one. Randomize the selected factions among the players and randomize their seating positions.

This book covers Atreides, Harkonnen, Emperor, Spacing Guild, Fremen, Bene Gesserit, Bene Tleilax and Ixians. Give each player their faction pieces, shield and faction rules. Leave unused factions out of play.

2. Set out the shared area

Put the board in the center and the turn marker on turn one. Place each faction marker at its seat around the storm track. Keep the Spice Bank, Tanks and battle wheels within reach.

Leave space for draw decks and discards. Prepare Treachery, Traitor, Fate Indicator, Nexus and Spice cards. With Fremen, prepare the six Storm cards. Keep the Supplies cache outside the Treachery draw deck.

3. Prepare the cards

Use the Dreamrules Treachery deck. Compared with GF9, remove Shield Snooper, Poison Blade, Amal, Thumper, Harvester, Artillery Strike and Poison Tooth. Add two Mercenaries, Supplies, Break Conditioning and Orange Catholic Bible.

The six Fate Indicators correspond to the six worthless cards. Orange Catholic Bible is not a Fate match. The Nexus deck contains one card of each number from one through seven and three blanks.

4. Set aside special pieces

Set aside the seven standard tech tokens. None starts with a faction. Keep the Atreides Carryall separate for its Fate. Put the Shield Wall markers within reach. Fremen take two Thumpers; Ixians take the Hidden Mobile Surveyor.

5. Prepare each player area

Keep available spice behind your shield. Leave space in front for a visible bribe pile and tech tokens. Keep living leaders and reserve troops apart from the Tanks.

Read your faction chapter and explain its public powers, including Fate and alliance abilities. No deals may be made during setup. Ignore abilities of factions that are not playing.

Spice setup needs a ruling

The v0.8 inventory lists fifteen Spice Blow cards, five Spice Mine cards and six Shai-Hulud cards. Its shuffle recipe uses only five worms. The current Fremen sheet also refers to two draw decks, while the setup text describes one. Questions #1837 and #1838 cover these conflicts. This draft does not invent a final shuffle recipe.

title: Prepare the game

text:
SET UP THE FACTIONS
6. Starting spice and Prediction

Give each faction its starting spice and troops. The starting amounts and free revival allowance are listed in each faction chapter. Place the Atreides, Harkonnen and Guild starting troops. Keep reserves behind the appropriate player shield.

Bene Gesserit secretly records a predicted faction and turn before Traitor cards are dealt. Do not reveal the prediction.

7. Choose traitors

Deal four Traitor cards to each faction except Bene Tleilax. Normally, choose one enemy leader as your traitor and return the other cards. Harkonnen keeps all four.

If Harkonnen draws two or more of its own leaders, or three or more leaders from one faction, it may require everyone to redraw. If a faction that must choose a traitor receives only its own leaders, reveal the problem and have everyone redraw. You cannot choose your own leader as your traitor.

When Bene Tleilax plays, keep each faction's unchosen cards separate for the Infiltration setup. Do not leave these cards with their original players.

8. Bene Tleilax cards

In the v0.8 six-player setup, take one card from each other faction's unchosen traitors. If Harkonnen plays, take its contribution from undealt cards instead. Bene Tleilax chooses one of the five cards as its traitor; the other four are Face Dancer cards. Shuffle the remaining cards into its Face Dancer deck.

9. Finish deployment

Fremen divides ten starting troops between False Wall West, False Wall South and Sietch Tabr. Its other ten troops remain in reserves.

Bene Gesserit places one troop in an unoccupied territory and one in the Polar Sink, leaving eighteen in reserves.

Ixians places the Hidden Mobile Surveyor in a non-stronghold territory, with three Cyborgs and three Suboids aboard. The remaining six Cyborgs and eight Suboids are in reserves.

10. Cards and the first storm

Give each player one Fate Indicator. Ixians may look at the initial Treachery cards before they are dealt randomly. Each faction starts with one Treachery Card; Harkonnen receives its extra card.

Determine the initial storm position using the procedure on the Storm page. Prepare the Spice draw sequence once the conflicts in #1837 and #1838 are resolved. Setup then ends.

Player-count scope

The supplied Bene Tleilax setup produces five cards in a six-player game. A procedure for other player counts is tracked in #1860; use this setup for six players until it is settled.

A TURN
Ten phases

Play each phase in the order shown. Complete it for every faction before beginning the next. The game lasts at most ten turns.

Your faction changes the ordinary rule

The phase chapters explain what everyone normally does. A faction advantage changes that rule only where its text says so. Read the timing, conditions and alliance permission before using it.

Storm order

The storm identifies the first player. Continue counterclockwise around the table. Bidding, shipment and movement, and choosing battles use this order unless an ability changes it.

Make choices at the right time

Announce an action early enough for players to respond with any permitted card or advantage. "Before reveal" means before opponents lose the opportunity to react. Do not rush a declaration into the instant of reveal.

Private information

Keep cards and battle plans secret except where a rule permits or requires disclosure. During Bidding, announce hand sizes. Players may inspect the Treachery and Spice discards. Only Atreides may keep notes about Treachery Cards; the separate question about recording public deals is #1850.

At the end of the turn

Spice Collection brings in desert and stronghold income. Mentat collects bribes, provides its faction windows and checks victory. If nobody wins, advance the turn marker and begin Storm again.

title: A turn

text:
STORM
The first turn

Place the storm at a random sector. The standard GF9 method uses the two players whose markers are nearest either side of Storm Start. Each secretly dials a number from zero to twenty. Reveal both numbers, add them and count that many sectors counterclockwise from Storm Start. This is unchanged in Dreamrules.

Later turns

With Fremen in the game, reveal the prepared Storm card and move the storm counterclockwise by its number. Return the card, shuffle the Storm deck and prepare the next card face down. Fremen may inspect it.

Without Fremen, use the GF9 procedure: the two players who last used the battle wheels each secretly dial one, two or three. Reveal and add the numbers to determine movement.

Before the storm moves

Resolve Weather Control before Family Atomics. After the distance has been calculated, give players the opportunity to play Atomics, then move the storm. Fremen Planetology can modify the revealed Storm card as described in its faction chapter.

See Weather Control, page 67; Family Atomics, page 67
Bene Tleilax window

Infiltration belongs to Storm. Its exact position relative to storm reveal and movement remains under council review in #1835.

1
1
A sector of the planet

The storm covers the whole radial sector. A territory may have both covered and clear ground.

Storm damage

Troops in exposed sand sectors swept by the storm or under its final position die and go to the Tanks. Spice in swept sectors returns to the bank. The Imperial Basin is protected while the Shield Wall stands. Rock, intact strongholds and the Polar Sink provide shelter.

Fremen troops are immune, although Fremen may choose to let them die. Troops aboard the Hidden Mobile Surveyor are protected. When the storm destroys a spice mine, troops at that mine return to reserves instead of the Tanks. Atomics can remove the usual protection from a sietch.

Read storm order after movement

The player marker the storm next approaches counterclockwise identifies the first player. Continue counterclockwise around the table. The shipment chapter shows how a storm can divide a territory and block a route.

Activity under storm

Storm blocks ordinary movement into, out of or through its sector. In Dreamrules it does not itself prohibit battles or other game actions.

title: Storm

text:
NEXUS
Check for a Nexus

The Nexus deck contains ten cards: one each numbered 1 through 7, plus three blanks. After Storm, reveal the top card. A number lower than the current turn number causes a Nexus. An equal or higher number, or a blank, does nothing. Return the card and reshuffle after every draw, whether or not a Nexus occurs.

See Alliances, page 42
Alliances become more likely

No card can cause a Nexus on turn one. The chance increases by ten percentage points per turn until turn eight. From then on, all seven numbered cards qualify: a 70% chance each turn.

Make alliances public

An alliance has at most two factions. During a Nexus, players may break existing alliances and agree to new ones. Announce the result before continuing. Outside a Nexus, a deal does not create an alliance.

Example: equal is not lower

On turn 5, a 5 does nothing. A 4 causes a Nexus. In both cases return the card and reshuffle before the next turn.

Information and timing

Atreides may inspect the top card through Nexus Prescience. That information can help you plan, but alliances change only if the revealed card causes a Nexus.

Independent of worms

Resolve Nexus after Storm and before Spice Blow. A Shai-Hulud appearance does not create another Nexus. This separation lets worm frequency change without also changing alliance frequency.

title: Nexus

text:
SPICE BLOW
Spice creates a reason to move

Spice is the resource you spend on cards, revival, shipment and battle support. This phase places new supplies on Arrakis. Collecting them comes later, after movement and battle.

Read the revealed card

Identify whether it is an ordinary Spice Blow, a Spice Mine or Shai-Hulud. The following pages explain the different effects.

Place ordinary spice

Use the named territory and its printed Spice Blow symbol. Place the amount shown on the card in that sector, taking spice from the bank. If the symbol is in storm, place none.

Keep the card visible

Put the territory card in its discard pile. A normal worm threatens the preceding territory for that draw sequence. Keep the sequences distinguishable.

Draw setup awaiting confirmation

The sources disagree about one or two draw decks and list six worms while the setup recipe uses five. Questions #1837 and #1838 track the exact draw and preparation procedure. This draft explains the card effects without selecting a conflicting recipe.

1
1
Find the named territory

Hagga Basin is highlighted as a location example. Use the printed spice symbol on the playing board for the exact sector.

Example: reading a Spice Blow

If a card specifies eight spice, take eight from the bank. Its symbol determines the placement sector. Troops elsewhere in the same territory will not collect that pile unless they reach its sector.

Two different kinds of information

Fremen may inspect upcoming Spice cards through Spice Blow Knowledge. Atreides instead has Nexus Prescience. Seeing a card early does not change how its effect resolves.

15
title: Spice Blow

text:
SHAI-HULUD
Resolve the affected territory

An ordinary worm removes spice and devours exposed troops in its affected territory. Devoured troops go to the Tleilaxu Tanks. A destroyed mine uses the different return-to-reserves rule on the next page.

Devoured troops
→
Tleilaxu Tanks
Fremen ride instead

Shai-Hulud does not devour Fremen troops. Those troops may worm-ride to a territory on the map. The Fremen ally is also protected from being devoured; protection alone does not grant the Fremen riding advantage.

More than one worm

Fremen chooses where worms after the first appear. Its Worm Riding advantage allows those later appearances in rock and strongholds too, so Fremen troops can ride from them. Resolve the destination restrictions of the ability before moving.

Thumpers

Fremen starts with two Thumper tokens. After seeing the Spice Blow cards, it may discard one to call a riding worm to a sand or polar territory containing its troops. At most one Thumper may be used each turn.

A riding worm

A Thumper worm removes spice but does not devour troops. Treat it as the first worm of the phase, so the Worm Riding advantage can redirect worms drawn from cards.

Example: create the first worm

A Shai-Hulud card is revealed. Fremen spends a Thumper at a legal location containing its troops. The Thumper supplies the first worm; Fremen can now choose where the card-drawn worm appears.

Mark the Shield Wall

Add one Shield Wall marker for each Shai-Hulud card drawn. Thumpers do not add markers. At four markers the Shield Wall counts toward victory, without becoming an ordinary stronghold for shipping or occupation.

Continue the turn

Worms do not trigger a Nexus. Keep alliance changes in the separate Nexus phase. After completing Spice Blow, continue to CHOAM Charity.

16
title: Shai-Hulud

text:
SPICE MINES
A supply that stays on the board

A Spice Mine card creates a mine at its named site. Unlike an ordinary pile, the mine provides its fixed yield each turn and remains after collection. It never accumulates more than its set amount.

Five printed sites

Arsunt, Bight of the Cliff, Cielago East, Cielago West and Gara Kulon have mine sites. The earlier board reference locates them individually. Use the yield specified for that mine.

Destruction returns troops to reserves

Storm and Shai-Hulud destroy mines. Troops at the destroyed mine return to their faction reserves instead of dying. They do not need revival before they can return to the board.

At the destroyed mine
→
Reserves
Example: no revival cost

Three troops are at a mine when storm destroys it. Return all three to reserves. You may ship them in a later legal shipment, paying the normal shipping cost.

Atreides and Carryall

Arrakis Fiefdom can create a three-spice mine in a sand territory without a Spice Blow marker. The Fate also grants Carryall, which triggers when a mine sends troops to reserves. Its token-count interactions remain in #1845.

Replenishment timing

The fixed yield and cap are stated in v0.8. The exact point when a surviving mine is replenished, including uncollected spice, remains under review in #1859. Do not add a fresh full yield to an existing pile.

title: CHOAM Charity

text:
BIDDING
Prepare the auction

At the start of Bidding, announce how many Treachery Cards you hold. The normal hand limit is four; Harkonnen may hold eight. A faction with a full hand cannot bid.

Deal one card face down for each faction eligible to bid. There are windows for appropriate cards and abilities both before and after the number is determined, before the first auction begins. Orange Catholic Bible can be given to a player with hand space in either window.

Bid in order

The first eligible player in storm order opens the first auction with a bid of at least one spice or a pass. Continue around the table; each bidder raises the current bid or passes. When everyone else passes, the highest bidder pays and takes the card.

For the next card, begin with the next eligible player after the player who opened the previous auction. Recheck hand space as cards are acquired. Keep hand sizes public throughout Bidding.

Paying for a card

You cannot bid more than you can pay. An ally may agree to cover a shortfall. The Emperor may cover it with Shaddam's Favor. A promise of support must exist before an otherwise unaffordable bid.

Pay the Emperor when its Bidding Payments advantage applies; otherwise pay the bank. The Emperor pays the bank for its own purchases. Harkonnen receives its extra card after a purchase, subject to its hand limit.

End the phase

Stop when all offered cards have been sold, or when nobody bids on a card. Return the unsold cards to the top of the Treachery deck. The Emperor collects spice set aside for Shaddam's Favor at the end of Bidding. Revival follows.

Orange Catholic Bible

At the start of Bidding, you may give this card to a player with room in their hand. You may do so before or after the number of auction cards is determined.

Information before a bid

Atreides and Ixians can inspect cards in different ways. Emperor can help pay. The following page explains these windows and the difference between knowing a card and owning it.

19
title: Bidding

text:
INFORMATION DURING BIDDING
Atreides prescience

Atreides may look at each card as it comes up for bid. Other players do not automatically see it. Atreides may keep notes about Treachery Cards.

Information about an auction card can itself be traded. Bene Tleilax is allowed to buy binding information about cards up for bid, despite its normal restrictions on deals.

Ixian knowledge

At the beginning of Bidding, Ixians may inspect the whole batch. It may divide the batch into two piles as evenly as possible and choose which pile is auctioned first. This is information about the offered cards, not a right to choose who receives them.

Technology

Once per phase, before the first bid on a card, Ixians may replace that card with one from its hand. If Ixians did not split the batch, Atreides cannot inspect the card Ixians takes. If it did split the batch, Atreides may see that card.

Resolve this exchange before bidding on the replacement card. Do not mix it up with the separate once-per-turn card exchange between Ixians and its ally.

Shaddam's Favor

When another faction buys a card, the Emperor may put spice in front of its shield to reduce that faction's payment by the same amount. The Emperor collects this set-aside spice at the end of Bidding.

The Emperor can agree to cover a shortfall before a bid. This support is a faction ability and does not require a binding deal with Bene Tleilax.

Example: an affordable bid

You have three spice. The Emperor agrees to cover two through Shaddam's Favor, so you can bid five. If you win at five, you pay three and the Emperor sets aside two. It collects the set-aside amount at the end of Bidding.

Separate the decisions

First determine the cards offered. Then resolve any permitted information and exchange abilities before the first bid on the relevant card. Finally auction and pay for it.

Do not reveal a card to the whole table merely because one faction has permission to inspect it. Hand size is public during Bidding; card identity is not automatically public.

20
title: Information during Bidding

text:
REVIVAL
Revive your troops

You may normally revive up to three troops per turn. This total includes both free and paid revivals.

Take the free revivals allowed by your faction. Each additional normal troop costs two spice, paid to the Spice Bank. You can only revive troops that are in the Tanks.

Return revived troops to your reserves. They do not go directly onto the board, but may ship during the coming Shipment and Movement phase.

Faction exceptions

An Ixian Suboid costs one spice to revive; a Cyborg costs three. Only one Sardaukar and one Fedaykin may be revived per turn.

Bene Tleilax may raise a faction's troop revival limit from three to five. They receive one spice from the bank for each non-Tleilaxu troop revived, including free revivals, and collect the payments for other factions' leader revivals. They may set a price to revive one leader per faction per turn.

Bene Tleilax have no revival limits and pay half price, rounded up. Their own face-down leaders cost full price. Their ally shares the discount. Round each leader's cost separately; total the discounted troop cost before rounding. See the faction chapters for other revival abilities and their exceptions.

Revive your leaders

When you have one or fewer available leaders, you may begin reviving your leaders from the Tanks. You may normally revive one leader per turn, paying spice equal to that leader's strength. Continue until all your leaders have been revived.

A revived leader is available for battle and remains vulnerable to a traitor call. If killed again, place that leader face down in the Tanks. It cannot be revived again until your other revivable leaders have also been revived and killed again.

The leader revival is separate from your troop revival allowance. Faction abilities and cards can provide exceptions to these limits.

INTRODUCTION TO BATTLES
What battles are for

Battles decide which faction can remain in a contested territory. Use them to take strongholds and prevent other players from winning. A player with troops in three strongholds is contesting a win. If the other players do not prevent it, that player wins in the Mentat phase.

Battles also affect the spice economy. You can deny opponents spice collection, or attack to earn a spice bounty for killing an opposing leader and winning the battle. That bounty can make an attack cost-efficient. Even a defeat can serve your interests if securing victory costs your opponent valuable spice, troops or cards.

What winning means

There can be only one victor in a battle; the two sides cannot share a victory. In an ordinary battle, the defeated faction loses all its troops in the territory. The victor also pays its battle costs and takes losses, so winning does not guarantee that it will have troops left to hold the territory.

Part of a battle	What it means


Battle plan

The strength committed by your troops. Spice can support troops to make them count more.




Leader

Weapons and defenses

	

Cards that threaten your opponent or protect your own leader.




Faction advantages

	

Abilities that affect the choices, information or outcome, at specified times.




Resolution and settlement

	

Determine the victor, then settle cards, rewards, payments and losses.

text:
ALLIANCES
Form or break an alliance

An alliance contains at most two factions. Alliances are public, and a faction can belong to only one at a time. During a Nexus, any faction may leave its current alliance and form another. Once that opportunity ends, wait for the next Nexus to change alliances.

The Nexus deck creates these opportunities in Dreamrules. Shai-Hulud does not create an additional alliance window.

Share a victory

A normal alliance needs four strongholds between its members at the victory check. Combine the positions each member controls. See the victory chapter for exceptions.

A temporary deal grants neither alliance powers nor shared strongholds.

Keep troops apart

Allies do not battle each other. You may ship into a territory containing your ally's troops, but must immediately leave during that same shipment-and-movement action. You cannot finish the action together. The Polar Sink and explicit faction exceptions, including Bene Gesserit advisors, allow coexistence.

If newly allied factions already share a territory, separate them during Shipment and movement. If the first ally to act does not leave, the second must leave or lose its troops there to the Tanks.

No binding deals between allies

Allies cannot make binding deals with each other. Their permitted assistance still applies.

What allies may share

You may discuss plans privately. Allies may show each other cards they have access to, including Treachery, Fate, Storm and Spice cards. They may not show each other Traitor or Prediction cards.

Allies may pay for each other's shipments and bids. A faction cannot make an unaffordable shipment or bid unless its ally has agreed to cover the shortfall. Other transfers or shared powers require a specific faction ability.

Alliance powers

Read both faction chapters. Shared Prescience and Shared Voice let an ally bring those powers into a battle. The Guild can extend shipping powers; Bene Tleilax extends its revival discount. Emperor can transfer spice immediately. Ixians can exchange a Treachery Card with its ally.

These are defined permissions, not a general right to use every power printed on an ally's sheet.

Example: paying for a shipment

Your shipment costs five spice and you have three. Your ally agrees to pay the remaining two, so you may make it. Without that commitment or another valid ability, you cannot ship first and hope someone pays afterward.

42
title: Alliances

text:
BINDING DEALS
Make the terms public

Factions that are not allied may make binding deals about legal actions, information and spice. State the terms aloud and agree to them. Once accepted, the deal must be honored. Both parties may agree to amend it.

Name who must do what, when they must do it and what payment is due. A discussion or an offer is not yet an agreement. No deals may be made during setup.

What you can promise

Information, a legal future action or a spice payment can be part of a deal. For example, a player can agree not to bid on one named card, to disclose information they are allowed to disclose, or to make a particular legal move.

A deal cannot authorize an illegal action, give away a faction power, or transfer cards, leaders or troops without a rule that allows that transfer.

Example: buying a pass

Before bidding begins on a particular card, two non-allied factions agree: "I pay you two spice now. You will not bid on this card." They announce and accept those terms. The recipient puts the spice in its bribe pile and passes for that card. The promise says nothing about the next auction.

Public terms and private discussion

Players may discuss plans privately. State publicly the terms that are to be binding; a private discussion is not a substitute for announcing the agreement. You can negotiate about information without revealing that information to everyone.

Make the agreement understandable

Restate unusual terms in plain language before accepting. Both players should be able to explain the same actions, payment and timing. If they describe different agreements, settle that difference first.

A clever bargain can reward careful play. Rushing through obscure wording or exploiting a language barrier makes it harder to play the game together.

text:
BRIBES AND PAYMENTS
Use a bribe pile

When you receive a spice bribe before Mentat, keep it outside your hidden supply. Collect the pile during Mentat. Until collection it cannot fund ordinary purchases, shipments or spice dialing.

You may use spice already in your bribe pile to bribe another faction. It moves to that faction's bribe pile and keeps the same delayed availability. Fremen's ally also uses this pile for spice returned through Desert Power.

Example: passing on a bribe

A gives B three spice before Mentat. B can pass two of those spice to C as another bribe. B has one waiting in its pile and C has two. Neither can spend that spice on an ordinary payment before collecting it.

A bribe is not an allied payment

Allies cannot make binding deals with each other. They may pay for each other's bids and shipments as the alliance rules permit. That payment goes to its normal recipient and is not a bribe waiting for Mentat.

The Emperor's ability to give spice instantly to its ally is a separate faction advantage.

See Alliances, page 42; Emperor, page 70
Follow the spice

Keep three things distinct: spice you can spend, bribes waiting outside your shield, and income waiting on tech tokens. Receiving spice does not always make it immediately spendable.

Example: payment now, spending later

During Bidding, Harkonnen pays Atreides three spice for permitted information. Atreides has two spice behind its shield. Until Mentat, its ordinary spending supply is still two, not five. It can pass the three-spice bribe onward in another bribe, but cannot use it to pay for a card.

Bene Tleilax

Bene Tleilax normally cannot give or receive bribes outside Mentat or make binding deals. Its exceptions include buying binding information about cards up for bid, and promising during Mentat to end a named Face Dancer Infiltration. Read its faction chapter before making a deal.

See Bene Tleilax, page 74
Token income

See Tech tokens, page 46

text:
MAKE THE AGREEMENT CLEAR
Specify the action

Name the move, bid or battle-plan choice being agreed. Check that each promised action is legal and that the players can perform it.

Example: arranging a battle

Two non-allied factions agree to a battle in which one will concede. They name the territory and specify that neither will play a weapon, call traitor or use Break Conditioning. The conceding player agrees to dial zero and use an available named leader.

They also specify the intended winner's leader and dial, making sure its strength will win. Any payment has an amount and a stated time. Both announce and accept the complete terms.

Resolve the battle normally

An agreement does not itself award a victory or remove losses. Players still make legal battle plans and resolve the battle. "A thrown fight" should not stand in for terms that the two players understand differently.

See Build your plans, page 33; Settle the battle, page 35
Changing your agreement

Both parties may agree to amend a binding deal. State the revised terms clearly. One player changing their mind is not an amendment.

Avoid binding deals that prevent players from trying to stop an imminent win. The v0.8 guidance treats these as poor sportsmanship. Using a faction advantage to make another player act first is part of play.

VICTORY AND THE SHIELD WALL
Count strongholds at Mentat

A lone faction normally wins with three strongholds. An alliance normally wins with four between its two members. You need troops controlling a stronghold at the victory check; visiting it earlier in the turn is not enough. Bene Gesserit advisors do not supply control.

The Hidden Mobile Surveyor is not a stronghold. Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Habbanya Sietch and Tuek's Sietch are the ordinary strongholds.

Shield Wall markers

Each Shai-Hulud card drawn adds one marker to the Shield Wall. Fremen Thumpers do not add markers. At four markers, the Shield Wall counts as a stronghold for victory only.

Its shipping price and occupation rules otherwise stay unchanged. If the storm divides it and two factions occupy separate parts at Mentat, the troops on the larger part control it for this purpose. Ixians cannot move the Surveyor through it once it has become a victory stronghold.

Tokens can contribute

A faction holding all three standard tech tokens gains one stronghold contribution. This and the Shield Wall can produce overlapping victory claims. Carryall counting is still under review in #1845.

Resolve overlapping claims

The v0.8 priority rule removes the tech-token contribution first if more than one faction would win. If more than one still qualifies, remove the Shield Wall contribution. Recheck the remaining ordinary strongholds.

The complete interaction with Prediction and Infiltration still needs an agreed procedure. #1847 and #1849 cover those cases, including an alliance with one or both members infiltrated.

Bene Gesserit can replace a predicted faction's win on the predicted turn. Its prediction does not apply to the Fremen special victory.

Bene Tleilax can share an infiltrated faction's win in place of that faction's ally, subject to the five-stronghold exception and the unresolved overlapping cases.

If no faction wins by the end of turn ten, Fremen wins. Its ally shares that win only if their alliance controls at least three strongholds. The Guild has no stallout victory.

Full-phase suppression

Stopping an advantage suppresses that advantage for the rest of the current phase. A single use does not stop every advantage of the faction. Suppression ends with the phase.

TRUTHTRANCE
Truth Trance

Quantity: 2

Publicly ask one player one yes-or-no question about the game. They must answer publicly and truthfully. The draw deck contains two Truthtrance cards.

Ask in public

Name one player and ask a single yes-or-no question about the game. They answer publicly. You may ask about information they hold or a future action to which they can commit.

Pause play for the answer

Playing Truthtrance pauses the game completely. Ask the question and obtain the answer before play continues. No binding deals, other cards or other game actions may occur during this pause. A second Truthtrance cannot interrupt it.

Use the right moment

You may play Truthtrance at any time. To constrain a battle plan, use it before commitment in the preparation window. Once plans are committed, a question does not grant permission to rewrite them.

Ask about a known fact

"Do you hold Stilgar as a traitor?"

The target knows its own Traitor Cards and can answer yes or no. The question reveals that fact to the whole table.

Name the card choice

"Will you play a poison weapon in our next battle this turn?"

The question names the choice and the battle. The target must give an answer it can fulfill under the information available to it.

An answer can bind future play

When the question concerns a future action, the answer is a commitment. The following pages explain how possibility, later events and conditions affect it.

59
title: Truthtrance

text:
TRUTHTRANCE: FUTURE COMMITMENTS
Answer what you can fulfill

At the time of the answer, it must be theoretically possible to fulfill it, however unlikely. Consider the information available to the answering faction, including its own cards, accessible deck information and earlier revelations.

Keep fulfillment possible

After answering, you may not deliberately take an action that makes your commitment impossible. You may take a risk that could cause it to become impossible later.

Risking a promised weapon

Bene Gesserit has promised to play a poison weapon in a later battle. It may use that weapon in an earlier fight if winning and keeping the card remains possible. It may not simply choose an action that guarantees the promised weapon becomes unavailable.

When later events make it impossible

If later events make fulfillment impossible, the answer no longer requires an impossible action. The v0.8 rule allows the player to proceed without announcing that the commitment can no longer be fulfilled.

Losing the weapon

In the earlier battle, Bene Gesserit loses its poison weapon. If there is then no possible way to fulfill the later commitment, it need not play a poison weapon it cannot obtain. Taking the earlier risk was allowed while fulfillment remained possible.

Keep the horizon short

A question about the next battle usually gives fewer opportunities for circumstances to change than one about a battle several turns away. Name the action and the relevant moment clearly.

Existing binding deals

Council ticket #1851 tracks conflicting wording about an answer that clashes with an existing binding deal. This chapter does not invent a precedence procedure. The other commitment rules here follow v0.8.

60
title: Truthtrance: future commitments

text:
TRUTHTRANCE: CLEAR QUESTIONS
Specify the subject now

Questions must concern the game. Do not ask about a future Truthtrance answer, or leave a person or choice to be specified after the target answers.

A forbidden future answer

"Will you answer yes to my next Truthtrance?"

This asks about a future Truthtrance answer, so the topic is forbidden.

A missing subject

"Will you ally with the faction I name afterward?"

The faction has not been specified. Name it in the question so the target knows what it is committing to.

Use questions the target can answer

Prefer information the target knows or actions it can choose. Avoid relying on another player's hidden cards or a remembered note being correct.

Conditions are part of the commitment

A conditional answer must be fulfilled only if its condition is fulfilled. Until fulfillment of the condition becomes impossible, the target must assume it will occur. Extra conditions give the target more ways for the commitment to cease applying.

A conditional battle question

"If you fight me in Carthag this turn, will you play a poison weapon?"

The target treats the battle condition as applicable while it remains possible. If you never enter Carthag and that battle cannot occur, the answer does not require a poison weapon elsewhere.

Finish the question before continuing

Atreides plays Truthtrance and asks Harkonnen a question. Harkonnen cannot play a card or make a binding deal before answering. No other faction may intervene with a game action either. Harkonnen gives its answer, then the game continues.

Clarity at the table

Ask slowly enough for the target and the table to understand the exact question. Clear wording makes the commitment easier to remember and apply.

66
title: Supplies and conditioning

text:
MOVEMENT, WEATHER AND INFLUENCE
Hajr

Quantity: 1

During your own turn in Shipment and movement, play Hajr to take one additional on-planet move. Move the same group again or another group, obeying normal restrictions. It grants no shipment and does not disqualify you from Zensunni Path.

Tleilaxu Ghola

Quantity: 1

Revive one leader or up to five troops for free, outside normal allowances. Troops return to reserves. A revived leader can fight again, including in another territory. During battle, play Ghola prior to reveal.

Weather Control

Quantity: 1

After turn one, play during Storm after the normal distance is known and before movement. Choose a counterclockwise movement of zero to ten sectors instead. Resolve this before Family Atomics.

Family Atomics

Quantity: 1

After turn one, play before storm movement. With a troop on or adjacent to the target, destroy the Shield Wall or expose one sietch to storm. Only Shield Wall detonation kills its occupants. Then remove this card from the game.

Orange Catholic Bible

Quantity: 1

Fills a weapon or defense slot with no effect. At the start of Bidding, give it to a player with hand space before or after the auction count is set. It does not activate Fate.

67
title: Movement, weather and influence

text:
HOUSE ATREIDES
House Atreides

Strategy: your first game

Keep a presence in Arrakeen for mobility and income. Buy a useful weapon or defense, but leave enough spice to move troops and support a battle.

Track the cards bought at auction. Before using Battle Prescience, decide which answer would actually change your plan. Fight when that information gives you an advantage.

Do not sacrifice troops just to rush the Kwisatz Haderach. Surviving troops and Leto's Tithe can be worth more than gaining it early.

Leaders
At start

10 troops in Arrakeen and 10 in reserves. Start with 10 spice.

Free revival: 2 troops.

Prescience and the Kwisatz Haderach

During Bidding, look at each Treachery Card as it comes up for bid. You may keep notes about these cards. Nexus Prescience lets you look at the top card of the Nexus Deck.

During battle, force your opponent to reveal one part of their plan early: weapon, defense, leader, or dial together with whether they are playing Mercenaries. Your ally may allow you to use this advantage in their battles.

After you have lost at least seven troops in battles, gain the Kwisatz Haderach. Play it with a leader in battles in one territory per turn. It adds two to the leader's strength and prevents that leader from being called traitor. A lasgun-shield explosion can kill the token; it can then be revived like a leader.

Before you gain the token, Leto's Tithe gives you two spice during Spice Collection if you control one stronghold, or three if you control at least two. Gaining the Kwisatz Haderach ends this income permanently.

Your Fate, Arrakis Fiefdom, may be played before Ship & Move. Gain the Carryall Tech Token, which you cannot lose. It triggers when a spice mine sends troops to reserves. You may also place a three-spice mine in a sand territory without a Spice Blow marker.

See Carryall, page 47; Mercenaries, page 65
68
title: House Atreides

text:
HOUSE HARKONNEN
House Harkonnen

Strategy: your first game

Use Carthag's mobility and your larger hand to threaten several opponents. Buy cards early, while keeping spice for shipment and battle support.

Check your traitors before choosing a target. A small battle can clear poor cards from your hand, but count the leader and troop losses before committing.

Your hand is only useful if you can afford to act. Avoid spending all your spice at auction. Treat Spite as a way to recover value from a bad result, not a reason to seek one.

Leaders
At start

10 troops in Carthag and 10 in reserves. Start with 10 spice.

Free revival: 2 troops.

Treachery, capture and Spite

Keep all four Traitor Cards during setup. If you draw at least two of your own leaders, or at least three leaders from one faction, you may call a mulligan that makes everyone redraw.

You may hold eight Treachery Cards. During setup, and whenever you buy a card, take an extra card from the top of the deck for free.

After winning a battle, you may randomly capture one of the loser's leaders. Exclude leaders already used elsewhere this turn. Kill the captured leader face down for two spice, or keep them for one use in combat. Return a surviving leader after that use. Return all captured leaders if you have no living Harkonnen leaders. A faction can always call its own leader traitor when you play that leader against it.

If your leader dies in battle, Vladimir's Spite lets you swap played Treachery Cards between the battle participants. Resolve the normal discards and returns after the swap. The winner cannot immediately discard a card you gave them. Spite does not change the winner.

A dead Cheap Hero, a traitor result or successful Break Conditioning does not trigger Spite. Cheap Hero cards cannot be swapped. Supplies eligibility is disputed in current production and awaits council question #1840.

You may call traitor in your ally's battles. Your Fate, Blackmail, forces your own or your ally's opponent to reveal their full battle plan early.

69
title: House Harkonnen

text:
EMPEROR
Emperor

Strategy: your first game

Use the first auction to build a useful hand, then establish a position you can afford to defend. Keep spice available for shipment and battle support.

Preserve your Sardaukar. They concentrate strength, but replace slowly and lose their advantage against Fremen. Avoid making Fremen your first target merely because it looks poor.

Look for an ally whose mobility, information or battle power gives your money a clear purpose. Fund a specific plan rather than paying whenever asked.

Leaders
At start

20 troops in reserves. Start with 10 spice.

Free revival: 1 troop.

Wealth and Sardaukar

When another faction buys a Treachery Card during Bidding, they pay the spice to you.

With Shaddam's Favor, place spice in front of your Player Shield to reduce another faction's bidding payment by that amount. Collect this spice at the end of Bidding. A faction may bid beyond its own available spice if you agree to cover the shortfall.

Your five starred troops are Sardaukar. Each has double the combat strength of a normal troop. Only one Sardaukar may be revived per turn. Against Fremen, treat Sardaukar as normal troops.

Your alliance advantage, Golden Lion Throne, lets you give spice to your ally instantly, at any time. This allows you to support payments such as revival and spice dialing that ordinary allies cannot pay directly for one another.

Your Fate, Prison Planet, revives up to five troops of any kind and any one leader at their normal cost. You may revive pieces for other players. The usual special-troop and leader limits do not apply to this revival, and Bene Tleilax does not collect income from it. You may play this Fate at any time except battle step 3.

70
title: Emperor

text:
SPACING GUILD
Spacing Guild

Strategy: your first game

Keep Tuek's Sietch earning while shipment income builds your options. Use discounted shipping to stay within reach of several strongholds.

For your first few turns, acting late is a useful default: see where opponents commit before choosing your destination. Change that plan when acting earlier secures an important position.

Retreat costs spice and does not guarantee your leader survives. Keep a reserve instead of treating it as free insurance. You must pursue a victory; there is no Guild stallout win.

Leaders
At start

5 troops in Tuek's Sietch and 15 troops in reserves. Start with 5 spice.

Free revival: 1 troop.

Shipment, timing and retreat

Other factions pay their shipping spice to you. Your own shipments cost half the normal rate. You may ship from reserves to one territory, from one territory to another at the destination's rate, or from a territory to reserves at stronghold rates.

Once during shipment and movement, choose one interjection: take your turn first, last or between other factions; swap your position with another faction; or make another faction act now and take its position. The last two choices must occur before your normal position has passed.

After battle plans are revealed, Retreat may let you ship troops to reserves at stronghold rates. Pay spice equal to your leader's strength for each played Treachery Card you save. Your leader still dies if the opposing cards would kill them. Pay spice committed to battle and retreat costs to the bank. Both leaders remain committed to the territory.

The live sheet prohibits Retreat once a traitor or Break Conditioning has resolved the battle. The precise order and all resulting losses await questions #1839 and #1841.

Your ally may use Discount Shipping. You may also allow Three Types of Shipment, including for Fremen. You can reveal spice from behind your shield to pay for your ally's shipment without losing that spice.

Your Fate, Battle Training, permanently lets you play two leaders in each battle, including Cheap Heroes. Either can be called traitor, and both survive or die together. Use the lower-strength leader to price saved cards when retreating. Play the Fate before shipment and movement.

71
title: Spacing Guild

text:
FREMEN
Fremen

Strategy: your first game

Build a useful combat hand without chasing every auction. Storm immunity and worm rides let you approach positions others cannot. Keep troops ready for the next opening.

Use Fanatical Tactics to preserve valuable cards, and protect your Fedaykin. Your turn-ten threat gives you bargaining power, but another faction can still win sooner.

Leaders
At start

10 troops distributed on the board (see setup). 10 in reserves. Start with 3 spice.

Free revival: 3 troops.

If nobody wins by the end of turn ten, you win. Your ally shares this win only if you jointly control at least three strongholds.

Life in the desert

Rally troops for free within two territories of the Great Flat. You cannot ship normally. Your troops move two territories and need no spice to fight at full strength. Your three Fedaykin have double strength; revive at most one per turn.

Your troops are immune to storm and may move into, through and out of it. You may choose to let them die in storm. Look at the top Storm card. The live sheet also permits inspection of both Spice Blow Decks; the deck structure is awaiting question #1837.

Shai-Hulud does not devour your troops. They may instead ride to any territory. If several worms appear, choose the locations of all after the first, including rock and stronghold territories from which your troops can ride.

Start with two Thumpers. After Spice Blow cards are revealed, spend at most one per turn to summon a riding worm to a sand or polar territory containing your troops. It eats spice but not troops. Treat it as the first worm of the phase when redirecting later worms.

With Fanatical Tactics, reveal a weapon, a defense or both in your battle plan early to retain it even if you lose. A traitor call against your leader or a lasgun-shield explosion still loses it. Spite may replace a protected card only with one of the same color. Supplies expiry is awaiting question #1842.

After all factions finish shipment and movement, Zensunni Path lets one faction, including yourself, make an on-planet move if it made none this phase. A Hajr move does not disqualify it.

Alliance and Fate

Your ally puts spice used for spice dialing into their bribe pile instead of the bank, and their troops are safe from worms.

Your Fate, Planetology, lets you add or subtract one from the revealed Storm card, starting in the Storm Phase when you play it and continuing each turn.

72
title: Fremen

text:
BENE GESSERIT
Bene Gesserit

Strategy: your first game

Spread advisors through accompanying shipments. Before turning them into fighters, decide what each group can achieve.

Use The Voice to protect your leader or remove an opponent's defense. Your troops revive slowly, so choose battles carefully. Pursue Prediction while building a position that can also win through strongholds.

Leaders
At start

1 in an unoccupied territory, 1 in the polar sink, 18 troops in reserves. 5 spice.

Free revival: 1 troop.

Secretly predict a faction and turn during setup. If it wins on that turn, you win instead. Prediction excludes Fremen's special victory.

The Voice and spiritual advisors

You always receive CHOAM Charity. You may use worthless cards as Karamas to stop a faction advantage, ship at half price while paying the bank, or buy a Treachery Card without paying.

Before battle plans are completed, The Voice can require or forbid a Treachery Card category, such as a projectile weapon, poison defense, worthless card or Mercenaries. Name special cards such as Lasgun or Weirding Way specifically. You cannot Voice Cheap Heroes. An opponent who lacks a required card silently ignores the instruction. You may also use The Voice in your ally's battles.

Fighters act as normal troops. Advisors can move and coexist with enemies or allies, but do not fight, count toward occupancy limits or control territory for ornithopters or victory. Each territory has one posture for your troops. Advisors entering a territory with your fighters become fighters.

When another faction moves into your territory, you may flip fighters to advisors. Reinforcement of a faction already there does not permit this.

At the beginning of shipment and movement, you may flip groups of advisors to fighters. A group with no other faction present flips automatically. This is the only window when an advisor territory becomes a fighter territory. You may ship either posture.

When another faction ships from off planet, place an advisor at its destination if you have no fighters there, or a fighter in the Polar Sink.

Political Marriages

Your Fate, Political Marriages, lets you use The Voice on one side in any or all battles where you have advisors that turn. Play it at the Voice window. Karama cannot stop this Voice.

73
title: Bene Gesserit

text:
BENE TLEILAX
Bene Tleilax

Strategy: your first game

Watch the Tanks and your Face Dancer cards before spending on expansion. Revival income and an available infiltration target can change which opponent you want to pressure.

Keep enough of your own leaders available for battles. Committing them to Infiltration has a cost even when the information is valuable.

Use Synthetic Spice to fund a shipment with a purpose. Killing reserves to land a troop that cannot achieve anything leaves you paying to rebuild. Check your deal restrictions before offering terms another faction could normally accept.

Leaders
At start

20 troops in reserves. Start with 10 spice.

Free revival: 0 troops.

Revival and synthetic spice

Dishonorable prevents you from giving or receiving bribes outside Mentat and from making binding deals, except buying information about cards up for bid. The live sheet also prohibits binding disclosure such as showing cards to other players. The special Mentat commitment to end Infiltration is described on the next page.

Collect one spice whenever a non-Tleilaxu troop is revived. Collect all spice paid for non-Tleilaxu leader revival. You may set the revival price of one leader per faction per turn, increase a faction's troop-revival limit from three to five, and inspect face-down leaders in the Tanks.

Your own revival has no limit. Pay half price, rounded up, except for your face-down leaders, who cost full price. Your ally shares these prices. Round each leader separately and round a group of revived troops after totaling its cost.

When shipping, you may kill troops in reserves to generate one spice per troop from the bank toward the shipment. This is Synthetic Spice.

Your Fate, Stone Burner, prevents all troops in one territory from being spice dialed for the rest of the phase, including Fremen. Play it during battle before step 3.

74
title: Bene Tleilax

text:
BENE TLEILAX: INFILTRATION
Face Dancers

During setup, receive five cards from other factions' unchosen traitors. Choose one as your traitor; the other four become Face Dancer Cards. Follow the dealing order in Set up the factions.

During Storm, you may revive a dead enemy leader matching a Face Dancer Card as a spy. Return that leader to its original faction. Commit one of your own leaders on top of the matching card as the impersonator. You cannot use your committed leader in battle.

The target may immediately call your committed leader traitor to prevent the Infiltration. That committed leader's traitor identity also applies to the revived spy, including your ability to call your own leader traitor.

While the revived leader lives and you retain its Face Dancer Card, you may inspect the infiltrated faction's spice and Treachery Cards at any time. Inspect its battle plan at the Infiltration window during commitment.

During Mentat, you may discard face down and redraw one Face Dancer Card. You may make a binding promise to reshuffle a specific Face Dancer then.

When an Infiltration ends, immediately draw a replacement Face Dancer so you again hold four. Put both the revived leader and your committed leader face down in the Tanks.

Zoal and shared victory

If Zoal is revealed in your plan, survives, and the enemy leader dies, you may choose Infiltration instead of the ordinary battle result. A traitor call can trigger this ability.

The opponent wins and loses nothing. You may keep your played Treachery Cards, return all your troops in the territory to reserves for free, and keep spice committed to the dial.

Set aside Zoal and the killed leader until next turn's Storm Phase. Then place the target leader in front of its faction's shield and Zoal among that faction's leaders. Zoal counts as the target leader in battle. Either Zoal or the target leader can be called traitor. Otherwise apply the ordinary Infiltration rules.

The live sheet says you share an infiltrated faction's victory in place of its ally, unless that alliance controls at least five strongholds. Cases involving two infiltrated allies and competing predictions need an explicit winner table. Questions #1847 and #1849 track those rulings.

75
title: Bene Tleilax: infiltration

text:
IXIANS
Ixians

Strategy: your first game

Keep Cyborgs and Suboids together when their combined movement and casualty options help. Avoid spending Cyborgs in fights that cheaper troops could handle.

Use your auction knowledge to improve your hand. Before exchanging a card through Technology, decide which missing weapon or defense matters most.

Plan the Surveyor's Mentat route before exposing troops outside it. Its shelter helps preserve an army, but troops aboard do not hold the surrounding territory. You still need troops outside it to claim strongholds.

Leaders
At start

3 Cyborgs & 3 Suboids in the HMS. 6 Cyborgs and 8 Suboids in Reserves. 10 spice.

Free revival: 1 troop, either Suboid or Cyborg.

Cards and augmented troops

Look at the initial Treachery Cards before they are dealt. At the start of Bidding, inspect the offered batch. You may divide it into two piles as evenly as possible and choose which pile is auctioned first.

Once per Bidding Phase, before the first bid on a card, Technology lets you replace it with a card from your hand. If you did not split the batch into piles, Atreides may not inspect the card you obtain.

Your nine Cyborgs have double combat strength, move two territories, collect three spice each and cost three spice to revive. Karama cannot affect Cyborgs.

Your eleven Suboids always fight at half strength and cannot be spice dialed. They cost one spice to revive and may move two territories when accompanied by a Cyborg.

If you win after dialing Cyborgs, undialed Suboids can die in their place. Those Cyborgs flip to their patched side. In a later battle, a patched Cyborg can be dialed once without dying and then flips back.

Once per turn, you and your ally may swap or transfer one Treachery Card. During battle, use the pre-plan exchange window.

Your Fate, Defect, prevents a special card from being used for the whole turn. Play it in advance or when a faction attempts to use that card, returning it to their hand. To stop Mercenaries or a special weapon or defense, act before battle plans are made. You cannot play Defect during battle step 3.

76
title: Ixians

text:
IXIANS: THE HIDDEN MOBILE SURVEYOR
A sheltered territory

During setup, place the Hidden Mobile Surveyor in any territory that is not a stronghold. Treat it as a territory within that territory. It is not itself a stronghold.

You may ship to the Surveyor at stronghold rates, and move into or out of it as a normal territory. Other factions cannot enter, including Bene Gesserit advisors.

Troops inside are safe from storm and Shai-Hulud. The Surveyor carries troops, not spice. It cannot pick up spice from territories it crosses.

During Mentat, move the Surveyor up to three non-stronghold territories. You may pick up and drop off Ixian troops along the route. Its movement can shelter troops before an approaching storm or worm.

The v0.8 Shield Wall rule prohibits the Surveyor from entering the Shield Wall after it becomes a stronghold for victory. Drawn Shai-Hulud cards add markers; Fremen Thumpers do not.

Plan the route before moving

First choose a route that stays within the Surveyor's movement allowance and avoids strongholds. Identify which Ixian troops you intend to pick up or drop off at each stop.

Troops left outside the Surveyor do not gain its protection. If you want a group protected from a coming worm or storm, it must actually be aboard when that danger resolves.

The Surveyor does not turn its surrounding territory into a stronghold and does not count as one for victory. Its stronghold shipping rate is a cost exception only.

Example: shelter aboard the Surveyor

The Surveyor travels through two legal territories during Mentat. It picks up your troops at the first and keeps them aboard at the second. Those troops occupy the Surveyor, not the exposed desert outside it. If you instead drop them in the second territory, they no longer have its shelter.

77
title: Ixians: the Hidden Mobile Surveyor

text:
GLOSSARY
Reserves and Tanks

Reserves are your troops available to enter play. The Tleilaxu Tanks hold dead troops and leaders awaiting revival. Returning to reserves is not the same as dying.

Territory and sector

A territory is a named area of the map. A sector is a radial slice used for storm position and spice collection. One territory can span several sectors. Count territories for ordinary movement distance, and state the sector where troops finish.

Control and occupation

Troops occupy the territory where they stand. Control matters for stronghold victory and some faction advantages. Bene Gesserit advisors can coexist in a territory without granting control, collection or ornithopters.

Storm order

Start with the player marker the storm next approaches counterclockwise, then continue around the table. Abilities such as Guild interjection can change the order of a particular phase.

Dial and support

Dial, troop strength, spice support and leader commitment are explained together on the following glossary page.

See Glossary: battle, page 79
Treachery, Traitor and Fate

Treachery Cards form your playable hand. A Traitor card identifies a leader you may betray. A Fate Indicator identifies the worthless card that activates your faction power.

Nexus

The phase after Storm. Draw from its deck; a number below the turn allows alliances to change. Return and reshuffle the card. Worms do not trigger Nexus.

Bribe pile

Spice waiting outside your supply until Mentat. You may pass it onward as a bribe but cannot spend it normally before collection.

Committed leader

A surviving leader used in battle is normally restricted to that territory for the Battle phase. A killed leader goes to the Tanks; if revived with Ghola, it can fight again. An ordinary traitor result does not commit leaders.

Infiltration

Bene Tleilax returns an enemy leader as a spy, gaining information and a possible shared victory. Face Dancer cards and Zoal establish it differently.

Tech token and spice mine

A tech token earns income when its event occurs. A spice mine is a persistent location with a fixed yield each turn.

78
title: Glossary

text:
GLOSSARY: BATTLE
Troop

One troop token. Its battle strength depends on its type and support. Count tokens separately from strength.

Dial

The troop strength committed on the battle wheel. Add surviving leader strength and permitted bonuses when resolving the battle.

Support

Spice spent to raise a troop from its unsupported strength to its supported strength. Ordinary troops cost 1 spice each to support.

Battle strength

The dial plus the surviving leader's strength and any permitted bonuses. Use this total to determine an ordinary winner.

Committed troop

A troop counted toward the battle dial. In an ordinary victory, take losses matching the dial and support spice. In an ordinary defeat, all troops in the territory die.

Committed leader

A surviving leader used in battle is normally restricted to that territory for the Battle phase. A killed leader goes to the Tanks; if revived with Ghola, it can fight again. An ordinary traitor result does not commit leaders.

Aggressor

The player currently resolving battles in storm order. The aggressor chooses the next battle and normally wins ties.

79
title: Glossary: battle

text:
ABOUT THIS DRAFT
A first reading draft

This book brings the current Dreamrules rules into one illustrated guide. It includes the eight finished factions, the revised card deck and the confirmed rulings used by the Dreamrules group. Iduali, Moritani and Ecaz remain playtest factions and are outside this ruleset.

Which sources it follows

Quickstart v0.8 is the starting point. Later confirmed Dreamrules rulings take precedence. Current faction sheets supply faction-specific details. GF9 supplies unchanged base rules. The original JSX rulebook informs the explanations, but its older phase sequence and experimental rules are not current authority.

Confirmed corrections

Truthtrance pauses game actions until its question is answered. Karama suppresses the named advantage for the full phase. A killed leader revived with Ghola can fight again; play Ghola before reveal. Allied troops may share a destination only for the immediate shipment-and-movement exception described in that chapter.

What still needs confirmation

Some sources disagree or leave an interaction incomplete. Those cases remain marked with their own council issue. A provisional answer is not a confirmed rule. The following page groups the open questions so a table can identify them before play.

Before your first game

Resolve the Spice deck preparation and draw-pile questions first. If relevant to your table, also check the Bene Tleilax setup outside six players and the turn-ten ending without Fremen. Agree any temporary table ruling openly; it does not settle the Dreamrules council question.

Questions and corrections

The council index is github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/1831. Each numbered question there has its own link, source evidence and eventual ruling. FAQ explanations belong in the ruleset rather than in this book.

How to read a draft note

The ordinary rule remains usable where it is clear. A note identifies the unresolved boundary; it does not grant permission to invent an exception. Update the affected chapter and examples together when a ruling is confirmed.
